topic: The complete AGENTS.md playbook — why an AGENTS.md generated by Copilot /init describes the code but decides nothing, and how a human edit adds business rules and a security section that stop an agent logging customer data.

title.main: The draft is true. It is not enough.
title.sub: /init describes the code. It decides nothing.

stages.title: /init writes a draft
stages.desc: Copilot scans the repo and drafts AGENTS.md from what it finds.
stages.narration: Copilot slash init drafts your AGENTS.md from the code it can see.

stages.title: What it cannot see
stages.desc: Business rules and security policy are not in the code. They are in people.
stages.narration: Business rules and security live in people, not code. The draft has none.

stages.title: Tuesday: an export button
stages.desc: An agent logs the whole order while debugging. The order holds a phone number.
stages.narration: Tuesday, an agent logs a whole order. Name, phone number, address.

stages.title: Wednesday: a promo
stages.desc: The discount is calculated inside the checkout widget, not in Promo.
stages.narration: Wednesday, a promo is priced in a widget, not in the domain.

stages.title: Audit the file
stages.desc: Count sections, vague lines, hard rules and security rules.
stages.narration: Audit the file. Count the hard rules, not the lines.

stages.title: Write the business rules
stages.desc: Totals from Cart. Promos through Promo.discountFor. Word for word.
stages.narration: Write down the business rules the team already knew.

stages.title: Write the security section
stages.desc: Never log names, phones or addresses. debugPrint counts as logging.
stages.narration: Add security: never log names, phones or addresses.

stages.title: Audit again
stages.desc: Nine sections, zero vague lines, fifteen hard rules, four security rules.
stages.narration: Run the audit again. Zero vague lines. Fifteen hard rules.

stages.title: Generate, then edit
stages.desc: Keep what /init got right. Add business rules and security by hand. Audit the file.
stages.narration: Generate the draft. Then write what only people know.

end.title: Generate the draft. Then write what only people know.
end.sub: Business rules and security are the sections no scan can infer.

post.caption:
Copilot /init drafts your AGENTS.md in seconds. Every line is true. That is the problem. 📄

It describes the code: stack, folders, packages. It decides nothing. In one week on a food delivery app:
• Tuesday, an agent logs a whole order while debugging: name, phone, address.
• Wednesday, a promo is priced inside the checkout widget instead of the domain.
Nothing in the generated file said not to.

AUDIT YOUR FILE
grep -c '^## ' AGENTS.md
grep -ciE 'best practice|clean code' AGENTS.md
grep -ciE 'never|must|do not' AGENTS.md

Sections, vague lines, hard rules. Aim for zero vague lines.

THE HUMAN EDIT
1. Keep the stack and folders /init got right.
2. Name ONE state pattern, not the two it found.
3. Write the business rules word for word.
4. Add a security section: never log names, phones or addresses. debugPrint counts.

Full playbook with a template: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/agents-md-complete-playbook

Follow for GitHub Copilot and AI coding tips.
